question: In the Johnson/Mazor study of paired grade II astrocytomas, how many temozolomide-treated patients developed hypermutated recurrences, and what was their outcome?
gold_notes: 6 of 10 TMZ-treated patients developed hypermutated recurrences, all progressing to GBM.

Now let me read the actual paper to get the specific details about the temozolomide-treated patients and their outcomes.Based on the Johnson/Mazor study of paired grade II astrocytomas, **6 of 10 temozolomide-treated patients developed hypermutated recurrences**, and **all 6 progressed to glioblastoma (GBM)**.

Specifically:

- **Number with hypermutation:** 6 out of 10 TMZ-treated patients
- **Mutation burden:** 31.9–90.9 mutations/Mb (vs. 0.2–4.5 mutations/Mb in initial tumors)
- **Mutational signature:** 97% of hypermutation mutations were C>T/G>A transitions at CpC and CpT dinucleotides—the canonical TMZ mutagenesis signature
- **Outcome:** All 6 hypermutated recurrences underwent **malignant progression to GBM**

The 6 hypermutated tumors acquired TMZ-signature driver mutations concentrated in the **RB and AKT–mTOR pathways**, including:
- [RB1](genes/RB1.html) splice-site mutations
- [CDKN2A](genes/CDKN2A.html) P114L mutations  
- [PIK3CA](genes/PIK3CA.html) E542K mutations
- [PTEN](genes/PTEN.html) A121T and G165R mutations
- [MTOR](genes/MTOR.html) S2215F mutations

The authors noted that mismatch-repair gene mutations (e.g., [MSH6](genes/MSH6.html)) and aberrant [MGMT](genes/MGMT.html) methylation were also acquired in the hypermutated recurrences, enabling continued TMZ-induced hypermutation [PMID:24336570](papers/24336570.html).

rag.answer:
Based on the Johnson et al. study (PMID:24336570), **6 of 10 temozolomide-treated patients developed hypermutated recurrences**, characterized by 31.9-90.9 mutations per megabase (compared to 0.2-4.5 mutations per Mb in initial tumors).

Regarding their outcome: **All six patients with hypermutated recurrences underwent malignant progression to glioblastoma (GBM), a high-grade tumor with a worse prognosis** (PMID:24336570). The hypermutated tumors harbored a distinctive mutational signature of C>T/G>A transitions at CpC and CpT dinucleotides, reflecting TMZ-induced mutagenesis. These tumors also acquired mutations in mismatch repair (MMR) genes and driver mutations in the RB and AKT-mTOR pathways that were not present in their initial tumors (PMID:24336570).
